result:
Round 457 is a **FAIL**: A stopped on a Medium finding (A-R457-REVIEW-M1) that B hasn't ruled on, and I reproduced it. I ran the short route for a stopped round, so C5, C6, C8, C9 and C10 were not run.

The rows I did run:

| Row | Result |
|---|---|
| C1 scope | Pass. Only the 6 granted paths changed, and doc 298 differs from `db95f40` on line 4 only. |
| C2 claims | Pass. The output from a clean `db95f40` clone and from the tree both match B's saved outputs, and stderr is empty. |
| C3 apply | Pass. All 4 sha256 checks are OK. |
| C4 covering tests | Pass. 4 files, 27 tests. |
| Probe replay | **Bug reproduced.** |
| C7 browser (Playwright Chromium, 1440 and 1280) | Pass. `/studio-lab` plays a 1-clip project and stops. Anonymous `/studio/middle-east` shows "Sign in required" with no audio or media loaded, so premium auth is not bypassed. |

**The bug:** the walker resolves `'~/lib/u/'` and `'~/lib/u/index'` to the sibling file `lib/u.ts` instead of the directory's `u/index.ts`. The directory's leaves are then never reached, and LT9 stays green. A's probe cases P4b and P5 are two more shapes of the same kind, and the replay matches A's saved output. A measured with `tsc` that TypeScript resolves these specifiers to the directory; I did not re-measure that.

Today it is latent: `app/` has one such sibling pair (`lib/utils.ts` and `lib/utils/index.ts`) and no importer uses a directory specifier.

B needs to choose between an LT9 invariant with an allow-list entry for that one pair, or a directory-only resolution flag. B also needs to rule on P4b and P5. The ruling text "`resolveSpecifier` can only add matches" is contradicted by the probe, and doc 299 carries the same sentence.

I started the mock API at `:5199` because it was down. Full vitest, typecheck, build, Biome and verify are gate rows and were not run. `browserVerified` is true, and the L57 checker exits 0.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- `c-round-457.md`
- `c-round-457.json`
- `c-round-457/c12-tree.json`
- `c-round-457/probe-replay.txt`
